source_note: Authored requirement summaries, not rulebook text. Visa Core Rules and the VCR dispute-condition guide are proprietary and are not reproduced here. Each entry cites the rule it summarises so a licensed copy can be checked against it. Every entry carries verified=false until reviewed against a licensed rulebook.

rules.title: Compelling Evidence 3.0 - prior undisputed transactions
rules.requirement: Two or more prior transactions by the same cardholder that were not disputed, settled at least 120 days and no more than 365 days before the disputed transaction.
rules.note: Qualification is checked deterministically in vakil.rules.ce3, not inferred. When it qualifies the issuer is obliged to accept the evidence, which is why it dominates the win model.

rules.title: Compelling Evidence 3.0 - matching identifiers
rules.requirement: At least two identifiers must match across the qualifying prior transactions and the disputed one: device ID, IP address, shipping address, or account/login ID.
rules.note: A missing identifier never counts as a match. Absence of evidence must not be scored as agreement.

rules.title: Delivery to the cardholder's address
rules.requirement: Proof that the goods were delivered to the address on the order, ideally signed for by the cardholder.

rules.title: Transaction and order record
rules.requirement: The order record showing what was purchased, when, for how much, and to which billing and shipping addresses.

rules.title: Proof of delivery
rules.requirement: Carrier documentation showing the merchandise was delivered, with the delivery date and the address it was delivered to. A signature strengthens the case considerably.
rules.note: The delivery address must match the order. A delivery to a different address is worse than no delivery proof, because it corroborates the cardholder.

rules.title: Proof of service for non-physical goods
rules.requirement: Where nothing is shipped, evidence the service was provided or the digital goods accessed - login records, usage logs, or download confirmations.
rules.note: Applies instead of shipping_proof when the order contains no physical item.

rules.title: Cancellation terms disclosed at purchase
rules.requirement: The recurring-billing terms and cancellation policy as they were presented to the cardholder at the time of purchase.

rules.title: Evidence no cancellation was received
rules.requirement: Records showing the cardholder did not cancel before the disputed billing date, or cancelled after it.

rules.title: Description matching what was supplied
rules.requirement: The product listing as it appeared at the time of purchase, alongside evidence of what was actually shipped.
rules.note: Rarely decisive. The cardholder's judgement of quality is subjective and documents seldom rebut it, which is why the win model prices 13.3 lowest.

citation.section: Not as described or defective merchandise

rules.title: Return policy and whether it was followed
rules.requirement: The return policy in force on the purchase date, and evidence of whether the cardholder attempted a return within it.

citation.section: Not as described or defective merchandise

rules.title: Proof the credit was processed
rules.requirement: Confirmation that the refund was issued, with the date, amount and destination.
rules.note: Close to decisive when present, and close to hopeless when absent. There is no argument to make if the credit genuinely was not processed.

rules.title: Refund policy disclosed at purchase
rules.requirement: Where no refund was owed, the policy as disclosed to the cardholder showing the sale was final.

rules.title: Two distinct transactions
rules.requirement: Records showing the two charges correspond to two separate orders, or that one was already refunded.
rules.note: The most winnable condition in the set, because it turns on records the merchant already holds.

rules.title: Rebuttal letter
rules.requirement: A written explanation of why the cardholder is not entitled to the refund, referring to the specific documents supplied.
rules.note: Applies to every dispute condition. This is the artefact vakil.draft generates, and the only one where a model writes text that is filed.

rules.title: VAMP dispute monitoring
rules.requirement: Visa monitors merchant dispute ratios and applies fines and review above programme thresholds. Disputes count toward the ratio when raised; a successful representment is not assumed to remove them.
rules.note: This is why pre-emptive refunds are modelled in a separate lane. See D4 in docs/DECISIONS.md. Programmes differ on removal; we take the conservative reading.
